content.content:
Web search results for query: "open source CLI redact secrets emails IP addresses from logs stdin stdout before pasting into LLM"

Links: [{"title":"leakguard 0.5.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/latest/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"ci: redact organization names, internal hosts, emails, and secrets in triaged issues by kolatts · Pull Request #504 · kolatts/pncli · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/kolatts/pncli/pull/504"},{"title":"GitHub - orshih6/ferret-scan: Find and redact sensitive data before it leaks — a fast, offline CLI and Go library that detects PII, secrets, and credentials in files and streams, scores them with context-aware confidence, and redacts them format-preserving. Nothing leaves your host. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/orshih6/ferret-scan"},{"title":"GitHub - sumankrsh/local-redact: Redact sensitive data before you paste it into an LLM. Runs in your browser; checksum-checked Gulf and Indian IDs. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/sumankrsh/local-redact"},{"title":"leakguard 0.1.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.1.0/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"leakguard 0.2.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.2.0/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"cleansh 0.1.4","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/cleansh/0.1.4/source/src/main.rs"},{"title":"leakguard 0.1.2","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.1.2/source/tests/integration.rs"},{"title":"GitHub - rog7/redact: Hide emails, API keys, and tokens in a log before you share it. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/rog7/redact"},{"title":"Crate cleansh","url":"https://docs.rs/cleansh/0.1.7/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/cleansh/"}]

The search turned up several open-source CLI tools that fit. The results don't show license details for most of them, so check each repo before relying on it.

- **leakguard** (Rust crate) looks like the closest match. It reads files or stdin and writes redacted text to stdout, covering emails, IPs, JWTs, and API keys. It also has a `--check` mode that exits non-zero when it finds something, which is useful as a gate before pasting. Fast, zero-dependency redaction of secrets and PII (emails, credit cards, IPs, JWTs, API keys, and more) from text and logs. Its docs show --mask char --only email,ipv4 for targeting specific types.
- **local-redact** (Python package and CLI) is aimed at exactly your use case. It handles stdin-to-stdout, writes a JSON report, and can restore the original values in the LLM's answer. Its README says it is a tool that finds email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, card numbers, ... IP addresses and API keys.
- **ferret-scan** (Go) is a single binary that detects PII, secrets, and IP markers in your files and streams. It sends redacted text to stdout and findings to stderr. It runs fully offline.
- **cleansh** (Rust) is built to sanitize terminal output for safe sharing. It masks emails, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, and tokens, and it accepts piped input such as docker or kubectl logs.
- **rog7/redact** (Python) is a smaller option. Its README describes a tool that hides secrets in a log before you paste it into Slack or a ticket.

## leakguard 1.0.0

**Repository:** https://github.com/ptukovar/leakguard

**License:** Dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option. The page states it is "Licensed under either of MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option."

**Install:**

```sh
# CLI
cargo install leakguard

# Library (Cargo.toml)
[dependencies]
leakguard = "1.0.0"
```

## CLI Usage

```sh
# Stdin to stdout: pipe a live log through it
tail -f app.log | leakguard

# Redact a file to stdout, keeping the last 4 characters
leakguard --mask partial --keep 4 access.log > clean.log

# Custom template masking
leakguard --mask template --template "<{LABEL}>" access.log

# Mask with a character instead of the default label
leakguard --only email,ipv4 --mask char --char '#' < input.txt

# Limit detection to specific kinds, or exclude one
leakguard --without phone app.log

# Allowlist safe values and redact custom words
leakguard --ignore 10.0.0.1,test@example.com app.log
leakguard --redact-word AcmeCorp --redact-literal "CUST-9981:CUSTOMER" app.log

# Print summary statistics to stderr
leakguard --stats app.log > clean.log

# Structured NDJSON findings (add --show-values to include matched text)
tail -f app.log | leakguard --json

# CI guard: exit 1 if secrets are found, with kinds and offsets on stderr
leakguard --check --verbose secrets-scan.txt || echo "found sensitive data!"

# List supported detector names
leakguard --list-kinds
```

Exit codes: 0 for success (including no findings under `--check`), 1 when `--check` finds a match, and 2 for a usage or I/O error.

## Supported Detection Types

Enabled by default:

- Email addresses
- Credit card numbers (Luhn-validated)
- IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
- JWTs
- US SSNs
- MAC addresses
- AWS access keys
- URLs with embedded credentials
- GitHub tokens (PAT, OAuth, app, refresh)
- Slack tokens
- Stripe keys
- Google API keys
- OpenAI keys
- PEM private keys
- IBANs (mod-97 validated)
- Azure storage connection strings
- Telegram bot tokens
- Discord tokens

Opt-in (more false-positive-prone, enabled through the library):

- `PhoneNumber`
- `HighEntropy` (generic secrets)

You can also add custom detectors through `FnDetector` in the library.

**License:** Apache-2.0, copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. It is an awslabs open-source project, and the full text is in LICENSE.txt. This page is a fork (orshih6/ferret-scan) of awslabs/ferret-scan.

**Install on Linux:** The page lists four methods:
- **Homebrew:** `brew tap awslabs/ferret-scan https://github.com/awslabs/ferret-scan && brew install awslabs/ferret-scan/ferret-scan`
- **pip:** `pip install ferret-scan`
- **Docker:** `docker pull public.ecr.aws/awslabs/ferret-scan:latest`
- **From source:** Clone the repo and run `go build ./cmd`. Use the Go version named in `.go-version`.

**Stdin-to-stdout redaction:**

```
echo "card 5500-0000-0000-0004 from jordan@example.com" | ferret-scan --stdin --enable-redaction
```

Redacted text goes to stdout, and findings go to stderr. To choose a strategy, use `--redaction-strategy` with `simple`, `format_preserving` (the default), or `synthetic`. For example:

```
cat customer-export.csv | ferret-scan --stdin --enable-redaction --redaction-strategy synthetic > safe-export.csv
```

**Detected types (relevant to your list):**
- **API keys, tokens, credentials:** The `SECRETS` validator uses entropy analysis and 40+ patterns, including AWS keys, GitHub tokens, and Stripe keys.
- **Email:** The `EMAIL` validator flags addresses and labels known corporate or SaaS domains as business.
- **IP addresses:** The `IP_ADDRESS` validator covers IPv4 and IPv6. It skips private, reserved, and test ranges and is gated by context keywords.

The page describes 19 validators in total, including credit cards, SSNs, bank accounts, phone numbers, and passports.

**Maturity:**
- **Stars, forks, watchers:** All show 0 on this fork. The page does not show the star count for the upstream awslabs repo.
- **Releases:** The Releases section appears empty in the captured page, so I can't confirm a published release from it. The pre-commit example references v1.10.0.
- **Activity:** The main branch has 988 commits, and the repo includes a changelog directory and a threat model document.

content.text:
Yes. My main pick is **leakguard**, a small Rust command-line tool licensed MIT/Apache-2.0. It's a plain stdin→stdout filter with built-in patterns for exactly what you listed, and it runs entirely on your machine. I haven't installed or tested it. Everything below comes from its published docs.

Assumption: you're on a regular Linux distro and can install Rust's `cargo` (or already have it).

## Main pick: leakguard

**Why it fits**
- With no setup, `leakguard < in.log > out.log` covers **emails, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, JWTs, AWS keys, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Google and OpenAI keys, PEM private keys, URLs with credentials embedded, and Discord/Telegram tokens**. It also catches credit cards, IBANs, SSNs and MAC addresses.
- It redacts **all** IPs, including private ones like 10.x and 192.168.x. Internal addresses in server logs are often the ones you want hidden.
- `--check` exits with status 1 if anything is found, so you can use it as a "safe to paste?" gate.

**Install**
```sh
# if you don't have Rust yet: your distro's package (e.g. `sudo apt install cargo`) or rustup
cargo install leakguard
# binary lands in ~/.cargo/bin — make sure that's on your PATH
```

**First run**
```sh
leakguard --list-kinds                      # see which detectors are on
echo 'user bob@corp.com from 10.0.0.7 key AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE' | leakguard
leakguard --stats server.log > clean.log    # stats go to stderr, clean text to stdout
leakguard --check clean.log && echo "nothing left"   # double-check the result
```
Useful options: `--only email,ipv4` limits it to certain types, `--ignore 127.0.0.1` keeps specific safe values, `--redact-word AcmeCorp` hides your own names, and `--mask partial --keep 4` leaves the last 4 characters visible so you can still tell values apart.

If you use X11, a handy pattern is `leakguard server.log | xclip -selection clipboard`. On Wayland, pipe to `wl-copy` instead.

**Caveat:** generic high-entropy secret detection (random strings without a known prefix, like `password=hunter2xyz` or custom tokens) is **opt-in and only available through the library, not the command-line tool**. Unusual secrets can get through. Read the output before you paste it.

## Alternatives

- **ferret-scan** (originally an AWS Labs project, Apache-2.0, Go). Install with `pip install ferret-scan` or Docker. Run it as `cat server.log | ferret-scan --stdin --enable-redaction > clean.log`. It writes redacted text to stdout and findings to stderr. It's more thorough on generic secrets (entropy analysis plus 40+ patterns) and looks more mature. The catch for your case is that by default it **skips private/reserved IPs** and only flags IPs when certain keywords appear nearby.
- **cleansh** (Rust, `cargo install cleansh`). Made for cleaning up terminal output you pipe into it, like `kubectl logs … | cleansh`. It masks emails, IPv4/IPv6 addresses and tokens.
- **local-redact** (Python). Works stdin→stdout and can put the original values back into the AI's answer afterward. That's handy if the reply refers to the placeholders.

One note on how I found these: I checked pickfit, the curated catalog of tested tools I have access to, and it had nothing that matches this job. The picks above come from a web search and the projects' own docs, not from a test install. Before relying on any of them, run a sample log with known fake secrets through it and check what gets missed.

Sources:
- [leakguard on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/latest) / [repo](https://github.com/ptukovar/leakguard)
- [ferret-scan](https://github.com/orshih6/ferret-scan) (fork of awslabs/ferret-scan)
- [cleansh](https://docs.rs/cleansh/0.1.7/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/cleansh/)
- [local-redact](https://github.com/sumankrsh/local-redact)
- [rog7/redact](https://github.com/rog7/redact)
